lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Okay, imagine this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Scientists take sixteen people and make them eat a thousand extra calories every day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's roughly an extra burger, fries and a drink. Every single day. For eight weeks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody goes to the gym. Nobody does anything special.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You'd think everyone gains the same, right?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nope. Some people gained about ten times more fat than others.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Same food. Same eight weeks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So what was different about the ones who stayed skinny?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Their bodies started moving more. Without them even noticing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Shaking their leg. Standing up more. Walking around.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One person was burning almost seven hundred extra calories a day, just from that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Their body burned off a big chunk of the extra food.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If you're the guy who says "bro, I eat so much and I still don't gain", this video is for you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three reasons you're skinny. And a simple plan to fix it, at home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Quick thing first: we're not doctors. If you're losing weight without trying, get checked by one.

lines.speaker: skinny
lines.text: "Bro, I eat a LOT. I just have a fast metabolism."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Eating "a lot" is tricky.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You remember the big meals. That wedding. That pizza night. That time you finished two plates of biryani.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't remember the day you woke up late and skipped breakfast. Or the lunch that was just chips. Or the day you weren't hungry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your body doesn't care about your best day. It counts the whole week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And for most skinny guys, the whole week adds up to just enough to stay the same.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Why does this happen?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When you eat, your stomach stretches, and it basically texts your brain: "we're full, stop eating."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some people get that message early and loud.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So you eat a huge lunch, feel stuffed all afternoon, and dinner quietly gets smaller.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You're not lying when you say you eat a lot. You just don't eat a lot every day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Second reason. Think of your daily energy like your phone battery.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most of it goes to just keeping you alive. Your heart, your brain, keeping you warm.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small part goes to digesting food.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the rest goes to moving. Not just the gym. Walking to class, standing, fidgeting, pacing while you're on the phone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That last part is sneaky.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Remember the study? When people ate more, some of them started moving more automatically. They didn't plan it. Their body just did it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So when you eat a bit more for a few days and nothing happens, it's not that food "doesn't work" on you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your body is burning some of it off. You just need a little more than you think.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Third reason. And this is the big one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Muscle is expensive. Your body has to spend energy to build it, and energy to keep it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So it won't build any unless you give it a reason.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Think of your muscle like a building that's always being worked on.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One crew keeps building new parts. Another crew keeps tearing old parts down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If you don't train, both crews work at the same speed. Nothing changes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Training hard tells the builders to work faster. And food and protein are their bricks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And "training hard" means sets where, by the end, you can barely do another rep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That struggle is the message to your body: "we need more muscle."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No message, no new muscle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Eat a ton without training, and most of it just turns into fat.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: "Face it, bro. You're an ectomorph. You were born skinny."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That "ectomorph" thing comes from an old 1940s theory about body types and personality. Not from muscle science.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Genes do matter, though. In one study, five hundred eighty-five people did the exact same twelve-week arm workout.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some barely grew. A few grew their arm muscles by more than half.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But most people were somewhere in the middle. And they grew.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You won't know which one you are until you train properly, eat enough, and give it time. Most skinny guys quit way before they find out.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: "Easy. Dirty bulk. Eat everything!"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Not so fast. Your body can only build muscle at a certain speed. Anything extra just becomes fat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So you want a small extra amount of food, every day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A review of the research suggests gaining about a quarter to half a percent of your body weight per week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If you weigh sixty kilos, that's around one fifty to three hundred grams a week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Slow. Boring. Works.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: How do you know you're eating enough?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Weigh yourself every morning. After the toilet, before breakfast.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your weight will jump around every day. That's normal. Just look at the average for the week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If the average hasn't gone up in two weeks, add about three hundred calories a day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's a glass of milk and a banana. That's it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next, protein. Protein is the bricks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Scientists looked at forty-nine studies. Muscle gains stopped improving at about one point six grams of protein per kilo of body weight a day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So if you weigh sixty kilos, aim for about ninety-six grams a day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sounds like a lot? It's not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three eggs and toast for breakfast. Rice, dal and curd for lunch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Chicken or paneer with rotis for dinner. A handful of roasted chana as a snack.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Add the shake I'm about to show you, and you're there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If you get full fast, drink your calories.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Milk, a banana, two spoons of peanut butter, some oats. Blend it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's about six hundred forty calories and twenty-three grams of protein.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And it doesn't feel like eating a full meal. For skinny guys, that's a cheat code.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three more easy tricks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One. Add a spoon of oil or ghee to your rice or dal. About a hundred twenty calories, and you won't even notice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two. Keep peanuts around. A small handful is about one seventy.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three. Add one snack at the same time every day, like a sandwich after your workout. Habits beat motivation.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now the workout. Just three rules.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One. Make your sets hard. Stop when you've only got one to three reps left in you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two. Do about ten hard sets per muscle, every week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three. Train each muscle two or three times a week. Not once.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Good news if you don't have a gym.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Light weights build muscle too, as long as the set is hard enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your muscle doesn't know if it's lifting a dumbbell or your own body. It only feels how hard it's working.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here are six moves for your whole body. No equipment.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Push-ups, for your chest. Keep your body straight like a plank, elbows a bit in, not flared out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Door rows, for your back. Hold both handles of an open door, lean back, and pull your chest to the door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Split squats, for your legs. Front knee follows your toes. Go down slow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pike push-ups, for your shoulders. Hips up high, head goes down between your hands.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Single-leg glute bridges. Push through your heel and pause at the top.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And towel curls for your biceps, or chin-ups if you've got a bar. Keep your elbows by your sides.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Too hard? Every move has an easier version. Too easy? There's a harder one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: How do you level up?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Do three sets of eight to fifteen reps.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When you can do fifteen on all three sets, the move is too easy for you now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Switch to the harder version, or put some books in a backpack and wear it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: More reps, then a harder move. Like levelling up in a game.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two small things.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before each move, do one easy warm-up set.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And rest one to three minutes between sets. If you rush, the next set gets weak, and weak sets don't send the message.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And sleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In one study, just one night without sleep cut muscle building by eighteen percent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Staying up till 3am scrolling isn't free. Aim for seven to nine hours.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here's the whole plan. Screenshot this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three workouts a week: Monday, Wednesday, Friday. Six moves, three hard sets each.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Walk on the days in between.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Eat about three hundred extra calories a day, hit your protein, and drink the shake if you get full fast.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Weigh every morning, check the weekly average. If it's flat for two weeks, eat a bit more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What to expect.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first few weeks, you'll get stronger fast. That's mostly your brain learning the moves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Getting bigger takes longer. Give it twelve weeks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Take a photo on day one. You'll want it later.

lines.speaker: skinny
lines.text: "Won't I just get fat?"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A little fat comes with any bulk. That's normal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gain slowly, and most of it goes where you want.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If your belly grows way faster than your arms and chest, eat a little less.

lines.speaker: skinny
lines.text: "Do I need supplements?"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No. Food and training do the real work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If you want one, creatine is the most researched. It helps you build muscle when you train, and it's considered safe for healthy adults.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Protein powder is just food in a box. Useful, not required.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Got a health condition? Ask a doctor first.

lines.speaker: skinny
lines.text: "Can I still play football or do cardio?"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Yes. Sports and walking are great for you, and they won't stop you growing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They just burn energy. So on days you play, eat a bit more.

lines.speaker: skinny
lines.text: "So... eat a bit more, train hard, sleep. That's it?"

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: "That's it. For twelve weeks. Don't skip."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Drop your height, your weight, and your goal for the next twelve weeks in the comments.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We read them, and your questions become the next videos.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next time: why you run out of energy after ten seconds of sprinting.
